summary: The main article describes the synthesis and characterization of Ni single atoms on carbon nitride (NiSAC/CN) for visible-light-promoted C-N coupling. It includes 4 figures detailing catalyst characterization and mechanistic studies, and 3 tables summarizing optimization, aryl halide scope, and substrate scope for various amines and aryl bromides.

items.heading: Fig. 1
items.caption: (a) Representative TEM image, (b) EDS mapping image, (c) HAADF-STEM image, (d) Fourier transform of Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra (silver: Ni, grey: N, brown: C), and (e) Ni 2p XPS spectra of NiSAC/CN. (f) UV-vis spectra of CN and NiSAC/CN.
items.description: This figure provides a comprehensive characterization of the NiSAC/CN catalyst, showing its morphology, elemental distribution, local atomic structure, and optical properties.

items.heading: Table 1
items.caption: Control experiments on the model reaction a
items.description: This table lists control experiments for the C-N coupling of ethyl 4-bromobenzoate with pyrrolidine, identifying the necessity of light, Ni, and CN.

items.heading: Fig. 2
items.caption: The schematic picture of (a) NiSAC/CN and (b) semi-heterogeneous NiCl2 $ 6H2O and carbon nitride (blue, gray balls, and yellow sheets represent Ni atoms, Ni aggregates, and carbon nitride). (c) Comparison of yields under NiSAC/CN or semi-heterogeneous NiCl2 $ 6H2O and carbon nitride. (d) TEM image of carbon nitride after reaction under semi-heterogeneous system.
items.description: This figure compares the efficiency and stability of the single-atom catalyst versus a semi-heterogeneous system, highlighting the prevention of Ni aggregation.

items.heading: Fig. 3
items.caption: (a) Representative HAADF-STEM image, (b) Ni K-edge EXAFS spectra, and (c) XPS spectra of NiSAC/CN after the model reaction.
items.description: Post-reaction characterization data confirming that the Ni single atoms remain dispersed and maintain their oxidation state after catalysis.

items.heading: Fig. 4
items.caption: (a) Quasi in situ EPR spectra of the reaction mixture at 150 K under various conditions. (b) Emission quenching experiment using PL spectroscopy with various concentrations of pyrrolidine (inset: magni fi ed spectra). (c) Proposed mechanism of photoredox C -N coupling on NiSAC/CN.
items.description: Mechanistic study results including EPR and PL quenching data alongside the proposed Ni(0)/Ni(II)/Ni(III)/Ni(I) catalytic cycle.

items.description: Table showing the reaction yields for different aryl halides (iodide, bromide, and chloride) in the C-N coupling reaction.
